summary: The article provides a largely accurate overview of Patanjali Foods' Q1 FY27 results, including key financial figures and dividend details, aligning well with reported news. However, there are minor discrepancies in the exact percentage of profit increase and a potentially misleading statement regarding the tax-free nature of dividends.

claims.claim: Patanjali Foods reported an 86.7% year-on-year increase in net profit for the June quarter of FY27.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm an 86.7% increase in net profit for Q1 FY27.

claims.claim: The company's net profit reached ₹335.73 crore, significantly higher than the ₹180.36 crore in the corresponding period last year.
claims.note: The net profit figures for Q1 FY27 and the corresponding period last year are consistent across sources.

claims.claim: Revenue from operations hit a new all-time high of ₹11,337.45 crore for the quarter, a 29.3% rise year-on-year.
claims.note: The revenue figure and year-on-year increase are confirmed by multiple sources.

claims.claim: The board has declared a first interim dividend of ₹0.80 per equity share (40%) for FY27, on shares with a face value of ₹2 each.
claims.note: Official announcements confirm the interim dividend amount, percentage, and face value.

claims.claim: The company has also fixed August 21, 2026, as the record date to determine the eligibility of shareholders for this dividend, which will be paid on or before September 12, 2026.
claims.note: The record date and payment date for the interim dividend are confirmed by official sources.

claims.claim: If the total dividend from a company exceeds ₹10,000 in a financial year, the company is required to deduct TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) at 10% under Section 194.
claims.note: Section 194 of the Income Tax Act states that TDS at 10% is applicable if the dividend exceeds ₹10,000 in a financial year for resident shareholders, effective from FY 2025-26.

claims.claim: Since Rahul's dividend is ₹400, no TDS will be deducted by the company in this instance, but he must report this income in his Income Tax Return.
claims.note: TDS is applicable only if the dividend exceeds ₹10,000 (or ₹5,000 in previous FYs) in a financial year. Since ₹400 is below this threshold, no TDS would be deducted, but the income remains taxable.

article_title: Patanjali Foods' Q1 Profit Jumps 86% on Record Revenue: What Investors Need to Know
